hints: Expand $R\cos(2x + \alpha) = R\cos(2x)\cos\alpha - R\sin(2x)\sin\alpha$ and equate coefficients.
Calculate $R = \sqrt{3^2 + (\sqrt{3})^2}$ and $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ to find exact values.
walkthrough:
Expand the $R$-formula using the compound angle identity:
$$R\cos(2x + \alpha) = R\cos(2x)\cos\alpha - R\sin(2x)\sin\alpha$$

Calculate $\alpha$ by dividing the two equations:
$$\tan\alpha = \dfrac{R\sin\alpha}{R\cos\alpha} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
Since $0 < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$$

State the expression in $R$-form:
$$2\sqrt{3}\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$$
with $R = 2\sqrt{3}$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

hints: Substitute the $R$-form expression into the integrand and express $\dfrac{1}{\cos^2(2x + \pi/6)}$ as $\sec^2(2x + \pi/6)$.
Integrate $\sec^2(2x + \pi/6)$ to obtain $\dfrac{1}{2}\tan(2x + \pi/6)$, and evaluate between $x = 0$ and $x = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$.
walkthrough:
Simplify the integrand and write in terms of $\sec^2$:
$$\dfrac{3}{12\cos^2\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{4}\sec^2\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$$

Subtract lower limit from upper limit:
$$\text{Integral} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{24} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{24} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{24} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{24} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{12}$$
$$\left(\text{or } \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{3}}\right)$$
